Let's say that a technology for Bitcoin was developed to erase the trail of transaction history, while still being able to fully validate the total number of coins. Let's say everything was still provable mathematically, but we just didn't know where the coins came from.

This would enable full privacy for all users.

I'm sure everyone would agree this would be a fantastic feature for Bitcoin.

Now, let's say that we COULD implement this feature into Bitcoin Core, or it COULD be added it as a layer 2 feature.

Hypothetically, a company that has a lot of money and resources could employ existing Bitcoin developers NOT to upgrade Bitcoin Core and instead spend their time adding this feature as the layer 2 service, because the layer 2 service would be an opportunity to create extra income for the company by charging some fees for the service.

It's a completely legitimate business model. The company is smart because it saw a need and filled it with a service.

However, this is also an example of a conflict of interest.

As far as regular bitcoin users are concerned, it would be best if the feature was just added into the core software protocol.

If it could have been, and wasn't, then we have a good example of individuals succumbing to corruption resulting in leaving Bitcoin less feature rich because they got paid to do so.
Bitcoin Food for Thought (In regard to hypothetical bitcoin features and corruption)
And yes, I am aware that Zerocoin does exactly these privacy features. Fortunately those implementing Zerocoin have stated their desire to get these features merged into bitcoin's protocol some day.

Isn't it dangerous to change the bitcoin protocol. Bitcoin is sort of an implied contract that says I'm going to put value in this abstract resource, or I'm going to mine using this software in exchange for an abstract resource given the guarantee that everyone is going to continue this protocol forever.

Zerocoin while it is a better concept (when it is actually a thing) is also more difficult to explain to newcomers. People are only going to adopt bitcoin to the extent they can understand it. Altcoins with different behaviors are available. Having miners vote on the protocol is complete bullshit because what about the people who are invested in bitcoin. In essence I've payed for these people's mining costs. It's as if I did the mining. Investors should get a say because they are more directly impacted. Essentially there is no ethical way to make a democratic decision in this scenario. Even if one investor disagrees we are changing the rules for someone else's money. Blocksize is one thing but full change in protocol using completely different cryptographic concepts is another.

Well the alternative to improving the protocol is to leave it as is, and then when a new better protocol takes its place people will find themselves with a lot of worthless bitcoins. Unless they knew enough to see the shift coming.

It would be a exponential decay. The length of the decay would likely be orders of magnitude beyond the average time people hold for. Darkcoin (I refuse to call it anything else) is already superior to bitcoin. You don't see bitcoin's value dropping out of thin air. There are more abrupt factors to its value built right into the protocol like the halving. No body sees that as a moral issue and for certain Satoshi sure didn't.

I think there's value in doing such a thing as a layer 2, as it breaks some usecases (things that require transparency and/or accountability).
That said, if there's something that's obviously better other bitcoin developers and users will react to it. If they make it a layer 2 service anyway, other developers can still make it a core feature.
